name: limfinity-engineer
description: Limfinity 7 (RURO LIMS) engineer: external data incremental sync (WPS pull / run_script realtime push), 7.0 dashboard HTML rendering with pure-CSS charts, Taro quality-management miniprogram + self-hosted Supabase backend AND WeChat CloudBase backend (Limfinity /api + frp master_data sync, account/password login + WeChat-binding auth), Limfinity VM infrastructure ops (Ubuntu upgrade, PostgreSQL migration, static IP, VM Console, cleanup, logrotate), and WeChat DevTools CLI automation (headless open/cache/preview/upload, miniprogram-automator screenshot self-check for UI changes, custom-tab-bar fully-transparent root cause and fix), and N1 public tunnel (standalone frpc + Alibaba Cloud Caddy reverse proxy with a BasicAuth gateway) to expose internal Limfinity /api over an ICP-filed domain, plus the WeChat CloudBase cloud function limfinityProxy that syncs Limfinity schema/master data (dual-layer auth, self-signed SAN certs, wx-server-sdk set({data}) wrapping, 3s→60s function timeout). Also Plan C: a resident .56 Python script syncs Limfinity schema/master data into the local Supabase over the LAN (single DB, no cloud function, no N1 public tunnel), consumed read-only by the miniprogram over the ICP-filed public domain supabase.nc2h-bio.cn. Its public read path now runs over the existing Alibaba Cloud frp reverse tunnel: a dedicated frpc instance on a dual-connected relay host dials out to frps, while .56 stays fully passive and needs no public egress and no DingTalk-exemption. WireGuard is dead in this environment because .56 has no public egress at all (ECS wg show reports zero handshake since 2026-08-16). Key trap: the ECS security group does not expose the frp remotePort (8001/8088) publicly, so external port probes are always CLOSED even when the tunnel is perfectly healthy - always verify end-to-end over HTTPS instead. See references/supabase_sync.md section 9. Plan C also syncs Limfinity custom fields: they are NOT database columns (subject.attributes.keys only ever returns built-in columns), so field definitions come from SubjectType#properties (the Property model) and values come from subject.get_value(property.name), matching the set_value semantics. Reusable methodology: when a Limfinity API is unknown, do not brute-force guesses - return introspection instead (class name, attributes.keys, reflect_on_all_associations, sample association object keys, raw value head) so the next iteration pinpoints the correct path, and never fail silently with an empty result; this converged in three iterations (v6 guessed userfields, v7 guessed configuration, both wrong - v7 introspection revealed properties:has_many). Also note the Supabase upsert Prefer header must be resolution=merge-duplicates; merge-upsert is invalid, generates no ON CONFLICT clause, and degrades to a plain INSERT that throws 23505 only when the target table is non-empty, which can make a cron job fail silently for months while the data looks fine. See references/supabase_sync.md section 10; section 11 covers Supabase self-host ops (Envoy replaces Kong, docker compose service names only, Studio Basic Auth password change requires rebuilding api-gw, Chrome caches Basic Auth so verify in incognito). Also Plan C registers the Node resident poller (sync-health-poller.js) and the frpc tunnel as Windows services via nssm (auto-start on boot, self-heal on crash). Key PowerShell pitfall: nssm prints 'Can't open service!' to stderr when the service does not exist (this is normal), and the naive '2>$null' still triggers a NativeCommandError that aborts the script so 'nssm install' never runs; the fix is '2>&1 | Out-Null' plus a $LASTEXITCODE check. '&' is the call operator, not a statement separator. See references/supabase_sync.md section 12. Plan C also uploads Limfinity file attachments (21 file fields: equipment acceptance reports/photos, personnel job-descriptions) into Supabase Storage: a standalone upload worker decouples file upload from the 30-min master sync (merging it in caused >120s nginx proxy timeouts that broke the whole sync); FileProxy bytes are PUT to the internal .56:8000 Storage over the LAN (service_role bypasses Kong/JWT), public URLs written back into master_data.records; Encoding::CompatibilityError must be guarded with safe_str + deep_scrub; deployment runs a reach_probe first. See references/supabase_sync.md section 13. A Helper Script can serve BOTH a ScheduledScript (selected directly, no nginx 120s limit) and the run_script API (subject to that limit) from one single registration: never wrap a thin shell script that loops back through Net::HTTP to /api/run_script, because that re-enters the very nginx timeout you were trying to avoid. Parameterize timeouts/batch/total-time-budget via data[...] so the two entries get different limits without a code change. Because the API can only execute already-registered scripts (it cannot create or schedule them), every script edit needs a manual re-paste in the .46 admin, so scripts must be self-diagnosing: classify failures by root cause and record the returned value's class (not just a total count), so a single run reveals whether an error is retryable or structurally unfixable. To tell 'script not registered' from 'I called it wrong', run a known-registered script as a positive control. See references/run_script_push_sync.md section 8. IMPORTANT LIMIT to the dual-entry design: it only holds for lightweight scripts. A script that iterates over many Subject records (dozens or more) can ONLY run as an internal ScheduledScript - triggering it via /api/run_script always returns 504 regardless of parameters (verified with 137 records: even a minimal time_budget:5 still 504s). Root cause: the startup phase (loading Subject records through the Limfinity DSL/ORM) alone takes ~120s and hits nginx proxy_read_timeout, and an in-script time budget only bounds the business loop, not startup. Diagnostic: run once with minimal parameters; if it still 504s, parameter tuning is pointless and you must switch to internal execution. By contrast mini_sync_schema, which only iterates field definitions, returns success in seconds. Keep the cron interval larger than the worst-case single run (startup ~120s plus budget 240s), i.e. at least 10 minutes. Also: a stray lone CR inside an agent .md frontmatter description breaks YAML parsing (scanners treat CR as a line break); Python text mode hides it via universal newlines, so detect it in binary mode. Also: Taro build must rename dist (mv dist dist_prev) instead of rm -rf dist because the WorkBuddy safe-delete guard blocks bulk deletes over 50 files; Limfinity script runtime model (Helper library vs ScheduledScript entry, top-level scope rules, immediate-run is not cron) is in references/limfinity_script_runtime.md; expert-pack maintenance rules (four-file sync, YAML description pitfalls, bare-CR binary check) in references/expert_maintenance.md.
